title: tagteam-swl-1997b
label: kick Ass order (Mean Man and Basic Killer)

won.source: Already billed champions holding the belts to ringside on the promotion's earliest surviving card (17 October 1997); no document in this record shows the win itself.

note: Successfully defended in a three-way against the Canadian Connection and the Tex Mex Connection on the promotion's earliest surviving card.

title: ustv-swl-1997b
label: Night

won.source: The fed's own Friday Night Raw (17 October 1997): Night pinned Manhunter with the Nightfall powerbomb.

note: No later document in this record shows a further change.

title: ustv-swl-1997b
label: Gravedigger

won.source: The fed's own King of the Mats pay-per-view (24 May 1998): Gravedigger won the title from Mass Destruction with a low blow and a chokeslam.

note: No later document in this record shows a further change.

title: brawler-swl-1997b
label: American Heartthrob

won.source: The fed's own Friday Night Raw (17 October 1997): American Heartthrob pinned Mr. Excellent with the Heartbreaker Heartpunch to become the first-recorded SWL World Brawler Champion.

note: The title changes hands to Night off-page; no document in this record shows that change.

title: brawler-swl-1997b
label: Chaos Bill

won.source: Sharp Turn (28 February 1998): Chaos Bill pinned Night with the Hells Depth powerbomb.

note: Retained the title on a technicality after being knocked unconscious by Bone Harmen at the 1st Anniversary show (13 March 1998); the promotion's own president ruled no title change since the match ended by stoppage, not a pinfall.

won.source: Already billed champion entering Sharp Turn (28 February 1998); no document in this record shows the win itself.

title: lightweight-swl-1997b
label: Prodigy

won.source: Already billed champion entering Sharp Turn (28 February 1998); no document in this record shows the win itself.

note: Successfully defended against Mr. Mainevent at Sharp Turn; the title changes hands to Hyper Man off-page some time before the fed's own 27 June 1998 newsletter.

won.source: Billed by the fed's own newsletter (27 June 1998) as the champion Gene Hoffman defeated; no document in this record shows how or when Hyper Man himself won it.
The fed's own newsletter (issue 1, 27 June 1998): "Gene Hoffman defeated Hyper Man by pinfall to win the lightweight title", on an uncollected episode of Friday Night Raw.

title: heavyweight-swl-1997b
label: Mr. Justice

won.source: Sharp Turn (28 February 1998): Mr. Justice pinned Insanity with a powerbomb.

note: Attacked and laid out by a masked man moments after winning the title; the title changes hands to Mass Destruction off-page some time before the fed's own 27 June 1998 newsletter.

won.source: Already billed champion entering Sharp Turn (28 February 1998); no document in this record shows the win itself.

The fed's own newsletter (issue 1, 27 June 1998), reporting Mass Destruction as "the new SWL World Champion" after turning on Gravedigger and joining the kick Ass order at the fed's own Pay Per View, Warzone (21 June 1998); no document in this record shows the title actually changing hands at that event.

title: heavyweight-swl-1997b
label: American Heartthrob

won.source: The fed's own third-person "SWL History" newsletter (5 November 1997): "AH was the first ever Heavyweight Champ," a reign predating this record's own earliest surviving broadcast.

note: The promotion's first-ever recorded champion, per the fed's own history; lost the title to Sniper at a pay-per-view named in that same history and independently corroborated as an SWL event, "In Your Face: Heartbreak Hotel," which does not survive in the held record.

title: heavyweight-swl-1997b
label: Sniper

won.source: The fed's own third-person "SWL History" newsletter (5 November 1997), naming the pay-per-view "In Your Face: Heartbreak Hotel" as the site of the title change; the event does not survive in the held record.

note: Lost the title off-page to Mr. Excellent some time before 22 November 1997.

title: heavyweight-swl-1997b
label: Mr. Excellent

won.source: The character's own self-posted recruitment advertisement (22 November 1997), corroborated by the fed's own Monday Madness broadcast (1 December 1997), where he retains the title in a non-title handicap loss.

note: Recorded from the champion's own contemporary claim, corroborated by the fed's own broadcast defending it. Lost the title off-page to Insanity some time before the promotion's own In Your Face: Sharp Turn pay-per-view (28 February 1998), where Insanity already holds it entering the show.

title: heavyweight-swl-1997b
label: Insanity

won.source: The fed's own Ring Masters broadcast (22 March 1998): Insanity is introduced entering the main event already carrying the SWL World Heavyweight Title, having lost it to Mr. Justice at Sharp Turn (28 February 1998, already a reign of record on this title).

note: A second reign, won back off-page from Mr. Justice; retained in a no-contest at Ring Masters. Recorded as vacated when the champion announced his own firing from the promotion around 8 April 1998, on suspicion of spying for a rival federation; no document names his successor directly.

title: heavyweight-swl-1997b
label: "Arrogent" Anthony Mislan

won.source: The fed's own King of the Mats pay-per-view (24 May 1998), where Anthony Mislan enters already champion; won off-page some time after Insanity's own firing (circa 8 April 1998).

note: Retained at King of the Mats when the referee stopped his own challenger's match after Mislan's leg broke on the ring stairs; a stoppage win does not transfer the title, though a thirty-day defense clause is raised as a cliffhanger, unresolved in this record. The title changes hands off-page to Mass Destruction (already a reign of record) some time before the fed's own newsletter of 27 June 1998.

won.source: Already billed champion entering the promotion's earliest surviving card (17 October 1997); no document in this record shows the win itself.

title: ustv-swl-1997b
label: "Hardcore" Harley Robinson

won.source: The fed's own Monday Madness broadcast (1 December 1997), where Harley Robinson enters already champion, some time after Night's own reign (won 17 October 1997, already a reign of record on this title).

note: Retained against Big Rob Styles on Monday Madness with interference from his own corner. Lost the title off-page some time before the fed's own Ring Masters broadcast (22 March 1998), where Kraze (formerly Biggy) is billed champion.

title: ustv-swl-1997b
label: Kraze

won.source: The fed's own Ring Masters broadcast (22 March 1998), where Kraze (formerly Biggy) enters already champion.

note: Lost the title off-page some time before the fed's own King of the Mats pay-per-view (24 May 1998), where Mass Destruction is billed champion.

title: ustv-swl-1997b
label: Mass Destruction

won.source: The fed's own King of the Mats pay-per-view (24 May 1998), where Mass Destruction enters already champion.

note: Lost the title to Gravedigger at King of the Mats by a low blow and a chokeslam, with his own manager, Miss Demeanor, distracting the referee.

title: lightweight-swl-1997b
label: The Executioner

won.source: The fed's own Ring Masters broadcast (22 March 1998), where The Executioner enters already champion, after Prodigy's own reign (still champion through Sharp Turn, 28 February 1998, then vacated off-page per the existing reign of record on this title).

note: Retained in a no-contest against The Ruiner at Ring Masters, stopped by a debuting authority figure before a finish. No later document in this record shows a further change before the title passes, off-page and undated, to Hyper Man (already a reign of record on this title).

title: ustv-swl-1997b
label: Dynamite Dana

won.source: The fed's own Monday Madness broadcast (29 June 1998), recalling a three-way for the title among Dynamite Dana, Steve Rodman and Tony Arnold from the promotion's own early era; the fed's own Supremer Awards (20 June 1998) separately credits a June 1997 Rodman-Dana match as the promotion's own first Match of the Year.

note: The promotion's earliest recorded United States Television Title change, predating this record's own earliest surviving card (17 October 1997), where Manhunter already holds the belt; no document shows how or when the title passed from Dynamite Dana to Manhunter.

title: supremerstrap-swl-1997b
label: Kraze

won.source: Already billed champion by the fed's own Supremer Awards (20 June 1998); no document in this record shows the win itself.

note: Retained against Anthony Mislan at Warzone (21 June 1998) when an unlicensed guest referee's fast count was overturned and the restarted match ended in Mislan's favor by disqualification, which does not transfer a title; still champion carrying the belt into the fed's own Monday Madness broadcast (29 June 1998), the last show in this record.
